theorem_title: Guard-sensitive bound for one wanted traversal
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.wanted_time_le {h J K NL NR old threshold : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (shift : ℤ)
    (A : Finset α) (B : Finset β) (C : Finset γ)
    (a : α → ℤ) (b : β → ℤ) (c : γ → ℤ) (left right : ℕ → ℤ)
    (eL : Fin NL ≃ B) (eR : Fin NR ≃ C)
    (hvL : ∀ i : Fin NL, left i.val=b (eL i))
    (hvR : ∀ i : Fin NR, right i.val=c (eR i))
    (w : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawReporting.Wanted h J α) (D : ℕ → _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostLevelData.Catalog) (hK : K ≤ J)
    (hkey : w.1 ∈ A ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.globalModulus h J ∣
      (a w.1%(p : ℤ)+_root_.ThreeSum.RawIncidences.lift w.2.1*(p : ℤ)+shift)-_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.globalKey w.2.2) :
    let I := _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawIncidences.rawOn h J (p : ℤ) shift (A ×ˢ (B ×ˢ C)) a b c
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightReportingWanted.time p shift left right NL NR old threshold I w D K ≤
      _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.initialUnit h J D K+
        (if threshold < old+_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostFrontierLayout.rootMass I w then 0 else _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostFrontierLayout.rootMass I w*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.searchUnit h J D K) := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let actual left and right arrays be value-preserving enumerations of finite source sets $B,C$. Fix a wanted label from $A$ satisfying the exact lifted-key divisibility condition, a catalog family $D$, and depth $K\le J$. Let $m$ be its raw root mass, $o$ the previous cumulative mass, and $q$ the threshold. Then $$T_{\mathrm{wanted}}\le I(h,J,D,K)+\begin{cases}0&q<o+m,\\mS(h,J,D,K)&q\ge o+m,\end{cases}$$ where $I,S$ are the specified initialization and search units.

Retains the actual dense-guard condition in the execution cost. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
